text: Hello and welcome to the live commentary of the Premier League clash between Aston Villa and Everton at Villa Park.

Villa endured an opening day to forget on the road against Newcastle United, suffering a 5-1 defeat at the hands of the Magpies at St James' Park in the midst of losing Tyrone Mings to a serious knee injury.
Unai Emery now has to galvanise his team to kickstart their season on home soil.
Moussa Diaby made an impressive start to his Villa career with a fine strike on a tough afternoon for his team.
Emery will be looking for consistency from Diaby and the rest of his players in the final third to get off the mark.
Everton also had a setback on the opening day of the season at Goodison Park as Fulham left Merseyside with all three points.
Sean Dyche knows that his team are under pressure to deliver results to avoid being dragged into yet another relegation battle, having barely survived the past two seasons.
The form of Dominic Calvert-Lewin will be crucial as the Toffees have not been able to bolster their ranks with too many new recruits during the summer.
Villa have made only one change to their starting line-up from their defeat to Newcastle.
Mings has been ruled out for several months due to a knee injury and is replaced in the backline by Torres, who came on last week.
Emery keeps faith with the rest of the defence that conceded five goals, while summer signing Tielemans remains on the bench.
Everton have also made one change to their side that lost to Fulham.
Calvert-Lewin returns to fitness to lead the line as Maupay makes way for the Toffees.
Dyche resists the temptation to add Danjuma into the final third.
Keane and Tarkowski retain their places in the middle of defence ahead of Godfrey and Branthwaite.

Aston Villa are unbeaten in their eight Premier League meetings with Everton since their return to the division in 2019 (W6 D2), having lost five of their previous six against the Toffees before this.
We're under way at Villa Park.
Watkins breaks down the right flank and sends a low ball across the face of goal.
Digne collects in the inside-left channel, but sees his effort blocked behind by Garner.
Douglas Luiz sends the corner short to McGinn on the edge of the box, but he sees his cross deflected behind for another set-piece.
The home side have made a bright start to the contest and are looking to build a rhythm to put the visitors on the back foot.
Everton are trying to push on to the Villa defenders and midfielders in possession to prevent them from breaking upfield.
It's keeping the hosts penned in their own half for now.
OVER! Villa beat the press as McGinn drives forward into the final third.
He finds Watkins, who turns and offloads to Diaby on the edge of the box.
The forward shoots first-time on his left foot, only to blast his effort over the top.
Calvert-Lewin and Martinez collide as the forward competes in the air from a cross from Doucoure.
Both players require treatment.
Both Calvert-Lewin and Martinez are back to their feet.
The Everton forward came off worse in the incident, but is okay to continue.
Diaby finds space in the final third, but opts against the strike and offloads to Bailey.
The winger goes for the instant return to his team-mate, who does not expect and it loses possession.
Young wins the ball in the middle of the park and runs at the Villa defence.
Douglas Luiz pulls him back and goes into the book.
Garner sends the resulting free-kick into the box where Onana has a free header and sends into a dangerous area, but Doucoure is penalised for a foul on Watkins.
GOALLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLL!!!! MCGINN BREAKS THE DEADLOCK!!!! 1-0 VILLA!!!!! McGinn is on the spot in the box to turn the ball home and put Villa ahead.
Diaby raids with menace at the Everton defence before he feeds Bailey.
The winger raids to the byline and produces a fine cutback for McGinn to dispatch past Pickford.
Bailey gathers Diaby's offload and sends a precise cross into the six-yard box for McGinn to convert.
Iwobi has space down the left flank and works a cross into the middle, but Doucoure cannot guide his effort on the stretch with his left foot towards goal.

McGinn has scored his 11th Premier League goal, but the first to not be scored with his left foot, and his first not to be scored from outside the penalty area since April 2021 against Manchester City, having scored five in a row from range between that strike and today.
McGinn makes a bustling run down the left flank and coasts past Doucoure, but Patterson pokes the ball behind for a corner.
PENALTY TO VILLA! Pickford brings down Watkins as he tries to prevent the forward scoring from close range.
Patterson clears Watkins' effort off the line after he is wiped out by the England keeper, but the referee soon points to the spot.
Pickford takes his time preparing for the spot-kick and is booked for time-wasting.
GOALLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLL!!!!!!! DOUGLAS LUIZ CONVERTS!!!!! 2-0!!!! Villa double their lead as Douglas Luiz holds his nerve from 12 yards.
The Brazilian sends his effort low into the bottom-right corner.
Pickford guesses the right way, but the strike has enough power and precision to find the net.
Only Fulham (8) and Brighton (7) have conceded more penalty goals in the Premier League since the start of last season than Everton (6).
CHANCE! Bailey surges down the right flank and offloads to Douglas Luiz in the box.
The midfielder opts against a strike first-time and tees up Diaby to shoot, but Pickford gets down to save his strike.
Digne goes down under pressure in the Everton box from a barge from Patterson, but the referee is not interested in his appeal for a penalty.
Calvert-Lewin surges down the right flank and has options in the box.
However, he fails to beat the first defender with his delivery.
Since making his Premier League debut for Everton in 2017-18, no goalkeeper has given away more penalties in the competition than Pickford.
Digne pulls back Garner as the midfielder turns away from the full-back with ease.
He goes into the book.
OFF THE POST! Pickford keeps Everton in the game with a brilliant stop to turn a stunning volley from Diaby onto the post and out.
Digne delivers a precise cross to the back post for Diaby to shoot first-time.
He connects perfectly with his effort, only to see his strike palmed onto the post by the England keeper.
That could be an important moment in the game.
Calvert-Lewin goes down and his face appears to be swelling after his collision with Martinez earlier in the game.
He'll have to be withdrawn here.
Calvert-Lewin makes way for Danjuma after suffering a blow to the face earlier in the game.
Watkins attacks a cross from Digne at the back post, but collides with the frame as he desperately tries to steer the ball towards goal.
Torres was offside in the build-up anyway to add insult to injury.
The home side have control of the game as we approach half-time.
Emery will want to see out the half with his side in command.
Danjuma twists and turns down the left flank and he floats a cross into the middle.
Onana meets the ball the edge of the box, but can only head his attempt at Martinez.
There will be nine minutes of added time.
SAVE! Danjuma and Garner go for the give-and-go in the inside-right channel.
He opens up room to fire at goal towards the near post, but Martinez makes a solid stop to send the ball behind for a corner.
Patterson is played into space down the right flank, but he overhits his delivery into the middle so much so that it travels out for a throw-in on the opposite flank.
Watkins rolls away from Keane, who pulls him to the deck.
The Everton defender goes into the book.
Villa work the ball down the left flank where Digne angles a cross to the back post that just evades Bailey's head.
Gueye goes in late on McGinn and goes into the book.
HALF-TIME: ASTON VILLA 2-0 EVERTON
Aston Villa take a 2-0 lead into the break against Everton in their Premier League clash at Villa Park.
The home side took the lead after 18 minutes through John McGinn, who was on the spot to convert Leon Bailey's cross.
Douglas Luiz made it two from the penalty spot after Ollie Watkins was fouled in the box by Jordan Pickford.
Moussa Diaby was then denied by Pickford to prevent Villa notching a third.
Matters got worse for Everton when Dominic Calvert-Lewin was forced off with a head injury after colliding with Emiliano Martinez.
Sean Dyche and his team face a huge challenge to get back into the contest.
Villa have played excellent football and could have been out of sight.
Unai Emery will have been pleased with his side's performance, but will want a third goal early in the second period to kill off the game.
A change for the Toffees at the break as Dobbin replaces Gueye.
An attacking move from Dyche.
We're back under way at Villa Park.
Dobbin surges past Cash down the left flank and cuts the ball back into the middle.
It deflects towards Garner, who can only fire wide of the target.
Everton have lost 41 of their last 42 Premier League away games in which they trailed by 2+ goals at half-time, the only exception being a 3-3 draw at Man Utd in February 2021.
Iwobi tries to chase a long ball down the right flank and immediately clutches his hamstring.
It does not look good for the Everton winger.
Villa surge forward with Iwobi off the field.
Diaby works an offload to Kamara in the final third, but his effort is deflected over the top.
Maupay enters the action to replace the injured Iwobi.
GOALLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLL!!! BAILEY MAKES IT THREE!!!! 3-0!!!!! Everton switch off at the back from a long throw into the box and Bailey slams a half-volley through Pickford's legs.
Digne acts quickly on the left flank and throws the ball in long.
Keane can only slice his hurried clearance straight to Bailey, who holds his composure to complete the finish.
Aston Villa are unbeaten in their last eight Premier League matches when leading at half-time (W7, D1) dating back to 18th February 2023 against Arsenal (L2-4).
This record looks set to continue for Emery's men.
Tarkowski connects with a header from Garner's cross, but he can only loop his header harmlessly over the bar.
Villa can afford to relax now given their three-goal cushion.
Emery could not have wished for a better start to the half.
WIDE! Diaby surges at the Everton defence and threads a pass through to Watkins.
He clips his strike past the onrushing Pickford, but the ball trickles wide of the left post.
Danjuma probes down the left flank and forces a low ball into the box.
Patterson collects and goes for a drive at goal that is deflected wide of the target.
SAVE! Maupay latches onto a deep cross from Young's corner and shoots first-time, but his effort is saved by Martinez low to his right.
Maupay has gone 26 games without finding the net.
He almost ended his drought there, but Martinez was equal to it.
McGinn teases the ball through to Bailey in the inside-left channel, only to be denied by a solid challenge from Tarkowski.
The winger remains on the ground after the fact.
Bailey makes way for Tielemans in the final third after a fine performance.
Douglas Luiz is withdrawn for Coutinho in the Villa midfield.
Diego Carlos comes on to shore up the Villa defence for Diaby.
Only twice previously have Everton lost each of their first two league games in a season without scoring a single goal, doing so in 1952-53 in the second tier and 1955-56 in the top-flight.
Digne works the ball to Watkins, who offloads with a neat touch for Coutinho.
He shoots first-time on his right foot from 20 yards, but Pickford gets down to make a comfortable stop.
Coutinho offloads towards Watkins in the final third, but he takes a loose first touch and allows Patterson to nip in and win the ball.
Watkins keeps the ball in play down the left flank and has space to run at Keane.
The Everton defender does well and fends off the forward with ease.
The intensity has dropped after the raft of Villa changes.
After their 5-1 defeat to Newcastle last week, Emery will want his team to play the full 90 to a high standard.
Coutinho hits a reverse pass to Konsa on the charge down the right flank.
He has space, but loses possession to the backtracking Tarkowski.
Watkins makes way after a solid outing without finding the net.
Duran replaces the forward.

GOALLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLL!!!! DURAN MAKES AN INSTANT IMPACT!!!!! 4-0!!!!!!! Duran pounces on a mistake by Young from a throw-in and skips past Keane before slotting an effort past Pickford.
Young tries an ambitious long throw to reach Keane in the middle of the Everton defence.
He sells his team-mate short and Duran nips in and applies a cool finish to get off the mark in the campaign.
Villa have put the icing on the cake to their performance and have brought their goal difference back to zero after their defeat to Newcastle last week.
What a difference a week can make.
Duran scored only 50 seconds after being substituted on, the quickest an Aston Villa substitute has scored in a Premier League match since John Carew against Everton in October 2009 (46 seconds).
Coutinho lines up an ambitious strike from distance that sails over the bar.
He had space and time so who could blame him.
CLOSE! Danjuma twists and turns in the final third and shoots on his left foot.
A deflection off Diego Carlos' boot takes it just wide of the right post with Martinez beaten.
Coutinho takes an awkward fall under pressure and appears to pull his hamstring.
He remains down on the field and may need to make way.
Coutinho is helped to the sidelines and Archer replaces the Brazilian.
It does not look good for the Villa midfielder.
Patterson trips Digne as he cuts inside on the left flank and goes into the book.
There have been more than a few injuries in the game, which is a major concern for both managers at this early stage in the season.
Archer pulls back Danjuma and goes into the book.
There will be nine minutes of added time.
Konsa misjudges a clearance and sends the ball behind for a corner.
Fortunately for him, Villa are able to clear their lines from Danjuma's delivery.
Garner floats a free-kick into the box from the right flank, but Martinez comes through a crowd of players to make a comfortable claim.
Outside of a couple of moments from Danjuma, Villa have been comfortable at the back which will please Emery after their performance last week.
Onyango comes on for the dying stages to replace Doucoure for the visitors.
FULL-TIME: ASTON VILLA 4-0 EVERTON
Aston Villa get off the mark in their Premier League campaign with an emphatic 4-0 win over Everton at Villa Park.
John McGinn opened the scoring before Douglas Luiz added a second from the penalty spot after Ollie Watkins was fouled by Jordan Pickford.
Leon Bailey notched a third after the interval and substitute Jhon Duran put the icing on the cake with a cool finish.
It was the perfect response for Villa following their opening-day defeat at Newcastle, while Everton lose for the second week on the bounce.
Villa are next in action in the Europa Conference League against Hibernian on the road.
Everton face a crunch clash in their next Premier League game against Wolves at Goodison Park on Saturday.
Thanks for joining our commentary today.
Until next time, goodbye.
